abstract: INTRODUCTION: The Centiloid (CL) framework standardizes global amyloid-PET across radiotracers. While global scaling remains essential for participant selection, amyloid-targeting therapies require quantifying localized plaque removal. However, applying global equations regionally introduces systematic bias, particularly in subcortical structures where off-target binding alters non-specific background. METHODS: We extended the Centiloid framework regionally and voxel-wise using GAAIN datasets: Level-1 ([11C]PiB) and Level-2 paired [11C]PiB and fluorinated head-to-head cohorts ([18F]florbetaben, [18F]florbetapir, [18F]flutemetamol, and [18F]NAV4694). Level-1 defines the regional Centiloid scale using region-specific intercepts while fixing the global slope. Level-2 calibrates fluorinated tracer uptake to reference [11C]PiB SUVR using linear equations. We compared three slope-intercept models (Global, Regional-Intercept, and Regional) using information criteria and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). RESULTS: Regional-Intercept model was identified as optimal across all four radiotracers. In neocortical regions, Global and Regional-Intercept models showed high agreement across canonical lobes. In deep gray matter, global equations introduced large systematic offsets, with mean absolute conversion errors in the pallidum reaching 27.7 to 45.6 CL. The Regional-Intercept model eliminated this bias, reducing subcortical MAE on average below 15 CL while preserving a unified biological scale. DISCUSSION: Applying global Centiloid equations directly to regions introduces substantial bias in subcortical regions. With the Regional-Intercept model, the same Centiloid value corresponds to the same amyloid concentration across brain regions and radiotracers. This provides a reliable basis for cross- sectional regional evaluation, multi-tracer cohort pooling, tracking regional clearance, and mapping regional progression in clinical research.
